name: Knot problems become group-theoretic: knot groups (Dehn)
summary: Dehn took the fundamental group of a knot complement as the key invariant, treated knot questions as word problems, and used this to separate the two trefoils.

name: Lorentz group and Minkowski spacetime: group theory enters physics
summary: Poincare showed Lorentz transformations form a group, Einstein derived them from two postulates, and Minkowski gave a tensor form of electrodynamics and showed Newtonian gravity incompatible.

name: Markov chains
summary: Markov studied dependent trials and showed the law of large numbers extends to chains, later applying them to letter sequences.

name: Several complex variables and Hartogs
summary: Hartogs discovered phenomena, such as automatic extension of holomorphic functions, with no one-variable analogue.

name: Complex dynamics: iteration of rational functions (Julia and Fatou)
from: iteration theory of functional equations (Schroeder, Koenigs)
summary: Julia and Fatou independently studied iterated rational maps of the plane, introducing attractors, repellers and the sets now named after them.

name: Abstract topological spaces from point-set analysis
summary: Cantor's derived and open sets, Weierstrass's neighbourhoods and Frechet's metric spaces led Riesz and Hausdorff to topological spaces defined by neighbourhood axioms without distance.

name: Intuitionism
summary: Brouwer rejected the unrestricted law of excluded middle.

name: Normal numbers: measure and probability applied to digit expansions (Borel)
summary: Borel defined normal numbers by digit frequencies, proved almost every real is normal, and Sierpinski, Champernowne, Mahler, and Copeland and Erdos later gave explicit examples.

name: Brouwer topology
summary: Brouwer used simplicial approximation and degree to prove invariance of dimension and the fixed-point theorem.

name: Decision problems for groups (Dehn)
summary: Dehn posed word, conjugacy and isomorphism problems for finitely presented groups, motivated by topology.
